title: test(verify): five slow test files pay the boot's first load at module scope, and handle builds its second fixture without a registry reset
body:
Part of #23181
Clause-②: no

Slice 3 of the test-budget card: the `@objectstack/verify` row, 24 files. This PR measures all 24 and changes five of them, adds one new shared test helper, and classifies that helper in one repo gate script. Nothing published changes: `skip-changeset` applies by its criterion, because nothing in the package's `files[]` moves and `scripts/` ships in no package.

## What changed

- **New `packages/verify/src/boot-warm-up.testkit.ts`.** `warmUpBoot(opts, { requires })` boots a throwaway app (no objects, its own in-memory database), signs the seeded admin in, signs one member up, and stops. A test file calls it once at module scope (`await warmUpBoot(...)`), so the boot's first load is paid during collection instead of inside the first clocked `beforeAll` or `it`. That is the repo's clocked-window convention (AGENTS.md, Build & Test: "clocked windows measure behaviour, never loading"). The helper shares nothing a case asserts on.
- **Five row files call it**, each with the options (and `requires`) of its own first boot: `handle.test.ts` (`automation: true`), `automation-trigger-elevated-door.test.ts` and `action-flow-elevated-door.test.ts` (`automation: true`, `requires: ['automation', 'triggers']`), `harness.served-composition.test.ts` and `delete-behavior.test.ts` (defaults).
- **`handle.test.ts` also drops one redundant arrangement.** `freshHandleFixtureStack()` built its "configuration of its own" with `vi.resetModules()` and a re-import. That drops the whole module registry, so each call re-evaluated the fixture's entire graph and every lazy load of the boot after it. It now imports the fixture module alone under a specifier of its own (`./handle.fixture.js?instance=N`). The fixture's builder still runs once more, every nested definition is still new, and its imports resolve to the instances the file already holds. The two cases that use it went from 2045 to 2469 ms to 769 to 1010 ms.
- **`scripts/check-verify-stand-in-erasure.mjs` classifies the helper (patch round 1).** The stand-in erasure guard discovers every exported function in a non-test `packages/verify/src` file whose first parameter is a type the package declares and publishes, and `warmUpBoot(opts: BootOptions)` is one. It is added to `NOT_A_STAND_IN` with its reason: it takes the same `BootOptions` that `bootStack` takes, `index.ts` does not re-export it, it is absent from `dist`, and it checks nothing. The guard's discovery is unchanged. Unclassified, `pnpm check:verify-stand-in` exited 1 (reproduced at `121ac4d71`); classified, the guard and its `--self-test` exit 0 (2 guarded, 18 exempt, 10 call sites reached).

Unchanged: every `it`/`describe` title line (sha256 identical at `1a9d48813` and the head for all five files) and every `expect(` (77, 10, 13, 12 and 39, before and after). No timeout value moved. No test was removed or moved to another project.

## The row, measured before changing anything (H1)

Box: 4 vCPU, shared with sibling agents. Every run went through `os-verify-lock`. "Clocked" is the file line's duration in vitest's default reporter (hooks plus tests, collection excluded), the number CI's `report-test-timings.mjs` reads. Runs had `AI_AGENT` and `CLAUDECODE` unset, so vitest picks that reporter. "Isolated" means `vitest run --maxWorkers=2` on the file alone, at `1a9d48813`. The whole-package run is `pnpm --filter @objectstack/verify test` (41 files, 362 tests, 157.4 s). The warm-up probe column is an untracked copy of each file with a plain module-scope warm-up (boot plus sign-in, default options), one run each, deleted before any commit.

The card's readings are 2.5× to 5.1× the isolated ones (median about 3.8×), so H1 holds. Three files are over 10 s even isolated: `unique-scope` (19.3 s), `parent-write-reach` (15.9 s) and `delete-behavior` (10.4 s).

## Where the wall goes

A timing probe (untracked copies that time `bootStack`, `signIn`, `signUp`, `seed`, each family's `run…Proofs`, and every `node:crypto.scrypt` call; deleted before any commit) read the top three files:

| file | boots (ms) | proof runs (ms) | scrypt | the cases themselves | clocked |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|--:|--:|
| `unique-scope` | 8 boots, 10007 (first 3007; the rest 755 to 1251) | 7 runs, 9228 | 19 derivations, 2819 ms | 179 ms | 20599 ms |
| `parent-write-reach` | 3 boots, 4295 (first 2686; then 842, 767) | 3 runs, 11334, incl. 16 sign-ups and 13 sign-ins | 32 derivations, 3313 ms | 28 ms | 15674 ms |
| `delete-behavior` | 2 boots, 5270 (first 4218; then 1052) | 2 runs, 6285 | 4 derivations, 967 ms | 14 ms | 12083 ms |

- **H2 is falsified as stated.** The top three files already share one boot and one proof run per `describe`, and every case only reads that run. Each `describe` boots a different app, posture or database: the walled leg, the controls that seed a duplicate before the declaration arrives, and the attribution apps. A merged boot would change the reports whose summaries the cases assert. So there is no per-case redundant arrangement to share there.
- **H3 is falsified.** No row file has a module-level warm-up. In every file the first boot is 2 to 3 s slower than the later ones. That is first use, not the boot: the default datasource's drivers and better-auth's entries are imported lazily from inside the boot, sql.js compiles its WASM, and every path runs cold. It lands in the first clocked window. The warm-up probe removed 1.2 to 3.8 s from every one of the 24 files.
- **One redundant arrangement:** `handle.test.ts`'s registry reset, described above.
- **H4:** what remains in the top three files is the per-boot steady cost (about 0.75 to 1.25 s per `bootStack`, isolated) and the families' proof runs. That is source in the published package (`harness.ts`, the kernel boot, the runners), so it is reported, not edited (Acceptance notes).

**Which five files.** They were ranked by measured removable test-side cost: `handle` (3.8 s plus the registry reset), `automation-trigger-elevated-door` (2.6 s), `harness.served-composition` (2.5 s) and `action-flow-elevated-door` (2.3 s). Four files tie for fifth within 50 ms: `reference-shape` 2242, `delete-behavior` 2229, `harness.org-context` 2212 and `erasure` 2197 ms. The tie goes to the largest card reading, `delete-behavior` at 46.4 s.

## Before and after, per changed file

Interleaved A/B, three rounds: base bytes from an untracked copy of each file at `1a9d48813` (blob `df66cfeb96ee` for `handle.test.ts`), then the changed file, alternating, all through the lock.

| file | card (CI) | isolated before (ms) | isolated after (ms) | median | whole package (ms), one run each | projected CI at the file's own ratio |
|:--|--:|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `handle.test.ts` | 38.3 s | 10735 / 9524 / 9520 | 4474 / 4336 / 4290 | 9524 → **4336** (−54%) | 10263 → 5052 | about 17 s: **row not claimed** |
| `automation-trigger-elevated-door.test.ts` | 15.0 s | 4715 / 4328 / 4206 | 1564 / 1789 / 1616 | 4328 → **1616** (−63%) | 3833 → 2444 | about 5.6 s: **row claimed** |
| `action-flow-elevated-door.test.ts` | 13.6 s | 3966 / 4316 / 4223 | 1581 / 1562 / 1488 | 4223 → **1562** (−63%) | 3614 → 2400 | about 5.0 s: **row claimed** |
| `harness.served-composition.test.ts` | 23.2 s | 7308 / 7093 / 7660 | 5006 / 4844 / 5201 | 7308 → **5006** (−31%) | 6972 → 6173 | about 16 s: **row not claimed** |
| `delete-behavior.test.ts` | 46.4 s | 9817 / 9889 / 10021 | 8023 / 7673 / 8300 | 9889 → **8023** (−19%) | 11287 → 9756 | about 38 s: **row not claimed** |

The projections multiply the median after by the file's own card ÷ isolated-before ratio. They are estimates; the card's own pin, the next refresh list, decides.

**What the move costs.** The warm-up runs during collection, so each changed file's collection (vitest `import`) grew by 2.6 to 6.6 s isolated (median per file). Each file's whole isolated vitest `Duration` (collection plus clocked) moved by −1.6 s (`handle.test.ts`, whose registry reset was real work and is gone) to +3.9 s (the trigger door), by median of the three rounds: the warm-up's own boot, sign-in and sign-up are new work, so for four of the five files the total wall rose while the graded clocked time fell. The whole-package run went 157.4 s → 167.9 s, one run each on a shared box. The 36 unchanged files' summed file lines moved 185.6 s → 188.0 s in the same pair of runs, so the box load was similar, and most of the rise is the five warm-up boots in collection.

## Proof the changed files still fail when their subject breaks

There was one ablation per changed file, with the prediction written down before each run. The verify-source ablations ([A], [D], [E]) went through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` in wrap mode. Every restore was proven: blob equals HEAD, `git diff HEAD` empty, `git status --porcelain` clean.

- **[A] `handle.test.ts`.** Mutation: the handle's `tenancy` reader (`packages/verify/src/handle.ts`) answers a constant single posture. Predicted: 1 red. Observed: 1 failed / 23 passed. The red case was `reports the walled posture a multi-tenant boot runs under — same reader, other stack`, the case that boots the query-imported fresh fixture.
- **[B] `automation-trigger-elevated-door.test.ts`.** Mutation: runtime's `refusesElevatedSelfTriggeredStart` (`packages/runtime/src/flow-start-admission.ts`) always answers false. This suite reads runtime through `dist/`, so the run was: `--hold`, rebuild runtime, `ablation-dist-preflight` (marker present in 2 built files), test, restore by `git checkout HEAD --`, rebuild, preflight `--absent` (marker absent from all 6 built files, tree clean). Predicted: 7 red. Observed: 7 failed / 9 passed (the six REFUSED rows and the wire envelope).
- **[C] `action-flow-elevated-door.test.ts`.** Same mutation and build legs as [B]: the action door asks the same predicate. Predicted: 7 red. Observed: 7 failed / 9 passed.
- **[D] `harness.served-composition.test.ts`.** Mutation: `harness.ts` builds the analytics service without `resolveCapabilityArgument('analytics', …)`. Predicted: 2 red. Observed: 2 failed / 5 passed (the two declared-cube cases; the no-cube control stayed green).
- **[E] `delete-behavior.test.ts`.** Mutation: the family's `judge()` reads the cascade branch inverted (`packages/verify/src/delete-behavior.ts`). Predicted: 4 red. Observed: 4 failed / 4 passed (positive proof and summary; NEGATIVE control and its count; the derive cases, the observation case and the ATTRIBUTION control stayed green).

## Tests and gates

The test and typecheck readings below are at `121ac4d71`, a merge of `origin/main` `8d05456cb` into the branch. The gate readings are at `1d178dcfc`, the patch head, which changes one repo gate script and nothing a `@objectstack/verify` test reads.

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/verify test`: 41 files and 362 tests passed, exit 0. In that run the five changed files read 5052, 2444, 2400, 6173 and 9756 ms (`handle`, the two elevated doors, `served-composition`, `delete-behavior`).
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/verify typecheck`: exit 0. `tsc --noEmit` is clean, and `check:test-typecheck` is OK, with 0 entries in the debt ledger. All six changed files are in the `tsconfig.test.json` program (`tsc --listFilesOnly`: 1 hit each). The helper is also in the build config's program, and it is in no tsup entry.
- `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` at `1d178dcfc` derived 70 commands for the 7 changed paths (the gate script brings 20 families more than the 50 the six test paths derived at `121ac4d71`). After a full `turbo run build` (76/76 tasks, all cached) in the recreated worktree, all 70 exited 0. `--ran`: "70 derived, 70 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN." At `121ac4d71` the 50-command derivation had also reconciled 50 of 50 (`pnpm check:dual-build-cjs-loads` answered exit 3, PREREQUISITE NOT MET, until a full build, then exit 0).
- `origin/main` has since moved eight commits. One of them makes `dispatch-gates` name `check:durability-log-level` for some files; `pnpm check:durability-log-level` exits 0 at `1d178dcfc`.
- Lint, which `dispatch-gates` does not name: `pnpm exec eslint packages/verify scripts/check-verify-stand-in-erasure.mjs --no-inline-config` exits 0. The repo-wide `pnpm lint` is left to CI.
- `skip-changeset`: the package's `files[]` is `dist`, `README.md` and `CHANGELOG.md`. Strings unique to this change (`warmUpBoot`, `boot-warm-up`, `freshInstances`) have 0 hits there (grep exit 1). The control from source (`bootStackOnce`) hits `dist/index.js`, `index.cjs`, both `.d.ts` files, `README.md` and `CHANGELOG.md` (grep exit 0).
- Every family CI runs is read from this PR's own check runs.

## Acceptance notes

- **Rows claimed:** `automation-trigger-elevated-door.test.ts` and `action-flow-elevated-door.test.ts`. **Shrunk, not claimed:** `handle.test.ts`, `harness.served-composition.test.ts` and `delete-behavior.test.ts`. The other 19 rows are untouched here, and their numbers are in the table above.
- **The same one-line fix fits the other 19 files.** By the probe column and each file's own ratio, eight of them project under 10 s with a warm-up alone: `handle.observe-writes` (9.4 s, borderline), `handle.system-insert-delete`, `harness.host-resolution`, `handle.public-form-door`, `harness.artifact-door`, `handle.exemplar-deal-lifecycle`, `erasure-transaction-authorization` and `handle.automation-door`. A ninth, `handle.update-doors`, projects at 10.0 s. These are one-run probes; a later slice measures them properly. Not filed; the report carries the choice for the seat.
- **What a test change cannot reach in the top files.** `unique-scope` is 8 boots plus 7 proof runs, and `parent-write-reach` is 3 boots plus 3 proof runs that sign up 16 personas and sign in 13. That is the per-boot steady cost and the families' own behaviour, in `harness.ts` and the kernel boot. Observation only, not filed; the report's open question carries it.
- **Scrypt.** `parent-write-reach` pays 32 production-parameter derivations (3.3 s of 15.7 s) and `unique-scope` pays 19 (2.8 s of 20.6 s). Each sign-in right after its own sign-up or the admin seed re-derives the same password and salt. plugin-auth's scrypt-memo testkit answers exactly those, but it is package-private, and the seat's standing answer is one shared home, never a copy. Observation, not filed.
- The `AGENTS.md` sentence on the 10 s line gained "unless the file declares a measured budget with its class" today (merged into this branch from `main`). This PR declares no budget. Whether a stack boot per single-cause control fixture reads as that ruling's first class is a reading for the seat, not for this slice.
